- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.1) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — maintain slight upward bias to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5–7 day price range is narrow, assume mean reversion and adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average.
- If forecast spikes after a sharp price drop (e.g., 5–10% drop in 3–5 days), reduce the magnitude of the subsequent spike by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.2), smooth forecast transitions — avoid abrupt directional shifts that don’t align with sentiment momentum.
- If true outcome deviates from forecast by >5% in first 3–5 days, adjust next 5–7 day forecast downward if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
